title: Sydney Harbour Bridge
blurb: The steel through arch bridge across Sydney Harbour, opened 19 March 1932. Explore the 503 m arch ribs in 28 panels, the hangers, the 49 m deck, the four granite-faced pylons and the skewback foundations.

sourceUrls.label: Archive.org: The Story of the Sydney Harbour Bridge, 50th Anniversary

systems.name: Arch ribs
systems.description: The two 503 m steel arch ribs, each built in 28 panels of 18.28 m, rising 134 m above the harbour.

systems.name: Lateral bracing
systems.description: The cross-bracing tying the two arch ribs together against wind loads.

systems.name: Hangers
systems.description: The vertical hangers carrying the deck from the arch, from 7.3 m at the ends to 58.8 m at the crown.

systems.name: Deck
systems.description: The 49 m wide deck: road lanes, two rail tracks, a cycleway and a footway across the 1149 m bridge.

systems.name: Pylons
systems.description: The four decorative 89 m pylons, concrete faced with granite, standing on the abutment towers.

systems.name: Approach trestles
systems.description: The steel trestles carrying the approach spans on each shore.

systems.name: Foundations and bearings
systems.description: The concrete skewbacks founded in sandstone and the four main bearings taking 20,000 tonnes each.

systems.name: Parapets and beacon
systems.description: Deck parapets and the aircraft beacon at 141 m.
